p0.original: When a nation binds itself by treaty, either to permit the entry of certain goods from one foreign country which it prohibits from all others, or to exempt the goods of one country from duties to which it subjects those of all others, the country, or at least the merchants and manufacturers of the country, whose commerce is so favoured, must necessarily derive great advantage from the treaty. Those merchants and manufacturers enjoy a sort of monopoly in the country which is so indulgent to them. That country becomes a market, both more extensive and more advantageous for their goods: more extensive, because the goods of other nations being either excluded or subjected to heavier duties, it takes off a greater quantity of theirs; more advantageous, because the merchants of the favoured country, enjoying a sort of monopoly there, will often sell their goods for a better price than if exposed to the free competition of all other nations.
p0.zh: 当一国通过条约约束自己时,要么允许该国禁止所有其他国家的某些货物从外国入境,要么免除一国货物对其所有其他国家的货物所负的义务,即该国,或至少该国商业如此受青睐的商人和制造商,必须从条约中获得巨大利益。 这些商人和制造商在这个国家享有某种垄断,对他们如此宽容。 该国成为一个市场,对其货物来说既广泛又有利:范围更广,因为其他国家的货物要么被排除在外,要么被征收更重的关税,因此其货物被取走,其数量就更大;更有利,因为享有某种垄断地位的受优惠国家的商人往往比受到所有其他国家的自由竞争影响时,其货物将以更好的价格出售。

p1.original: Such treaties, however, though they may be advantageous to the merchants and manufacturers of the favoured, are necessarily disadvantageous to those of the favouring country. A monopoly is thus granted against them to a foreign nation; and they must frequently buy the foreign goods they have occasion for, dearer than if the free competition of other nations was admitted. That part of its own produce with which such a nation purchases foreign goods, must consequently be sold cheaper; because, when two things are exchanged for one another, the cheapness of the one is a necessary consequence, or rather is the same thing, with the dearness of the other. The exchangeable value of its annual produce, therefore, is likely to be diminished by every such treaty. This diminution, however, can scarce amount to any positive loss, but only to a lessening of the gain which it might otherwise make. Though it sells its goods cheaper than it otherwise might do, it will not probably sell them for less than they cost; nor, as in the case of bounties, for a price which will not replace the capital employed in bringing them to market, together with the ordinary profits of stock. The trade could not go on long if it did. Even the favouring country, therefore, may still gain by the trade, though less than if there was a free competition.
p1.zh: 然而,这类条约虽然可能有利于被优惠国的商人和制造商,但必然不利于被优惠国的商商和制造商。 因此,垄断权被授予一个外国;他们必须经常购买他们拥有的外国商品,比允许其他国家进行自由竞争还要重要。 因此,一国购买外国商品的那部分产品必须更便宜地出售;因为,当两个东西相互交换时,一个的廉价是必然的后果,或者说,是同一回事,而另一个的稀缺性。 因此,每个此类条约都有可能降低其年度产品的可交换价值。 然而,这种减少可能很少等于任何积极损失,而只是减少否则可能带来的收益。 尽管它出售其商品比其他商品便宜,但可能不会以低于成本的价格出售;也不象优惠那样,其价格不会取代用于将商品带入市场的资本以及股票的普通利润。 如果贸易真的如此,贸易不会持续太久。 因此,即使是有利国家也可能从贸易中获益,尽管比有自由竞争的情况要少。

p2.original: Some treaties of commerce, however, have been supposed advantageous, upon principles very different from these; and a commercial country has sometimes granted a monopoly of this kind, against itself, to certain goods of a foreign nation, because it expected, that in the whole commerce between them, it would annually sell more than it would buy, and that a balance in gold and silver would be annually returned to it. It is upon this principle that the treaty of commerce between England and Portugal, concluded in 1703 by Mr Methuen, has been so much commended. The following is a literal translation of that treaty, which consists of three articles only.
p2.zh: 然而,一些商业条约被认为有利,其原则与这些原则大不相同;一个商业国家有时对外国的某些货物给予这种垄断,因为它期望,在它们之间的整个商业中,它每年的销售额会超过它购买的销售额,而且每年将金银的余额归还给它。 正是根据这一原则,梅特洪先生于1703年缔结的英格兰和葡萄牙之间的商业条约受到了如此多的赞扬。 下面是该条约的字面翻译,它只包括三个条款。

p3.original: ART. I. His sacred royal majesty of Portugal promises, both in his own name and that of his successors, to admit for ever hereafter, into Portugal, the woollen cloths, and the rest of the woollen manufactures of the British, as was accustomed, till they were prohibited by the law; nevertheless upon this condition:
p3.zh: ART. (英语). 我从你那得到的。 他的神圣的葡萄牙王室以自己和继任者的名义承诺,今后将一如既往地承认加入葡萄牙,即英国的羊毛布和其余羊毛布的制造,直到法律禁止为止;然而,基于这一条件:

p4.original: ART. II. That is to say, that her sacred royal majesty of Great Britain shall, in her own name, and that of her successors, be obliged, for ever hereafter, to admit the wines of the growth of Portugal into Britain; so that at no time, whether there shall be peace or war between the kingdoms of Britain and France, any thing more shall be demanded for these wines by the name of custom or duty, or by whatsoever other title, directly or indirectly, whether they shall be imported into Great Britain in pipes or hogsheads, or other casks, than what shall be demanded for the like quantity or measure of French wine, deducting or abating a third part of the custom or duty. But if, at any time, this deduction or abatement of customs, which is to be made as aforesaid, shall in any manner be attempted and prejudiced, it shall be just and lawful for his sacred royal majesty of Portugal, again to prohibit the woollen cloths, and the rest of the British woollen manufactures.
p4.zh: ART. (英语). 二、导 言也就是说,她的神圣的英国王室陛下,以及她的继任者,必须永远以她本人的名义,将葡萄牙成长的葡萄酒接纳到英国;因此无论英国王国和法国王国之间何时会有和平或战争,无论这些葡萄酒的名称是习俗或义务,还是直接或间接地通过其他任何头衔,无论是用管道或猪头或其他水缸进口到英国,无论法国葡萄酒的数量或量,都要扣除或免除三分之一的风俗或义务,无论这些葡萄酒是何物。 但是,如果在任何时间,如上所述,这种对习俗的扣除或减轻,将受到任何企图和偏见,对他的神圣的葡萄牙王室来说,再次禁止羊毛布和英国羊毛布的制造,将是公正和合法的。

p5.original: ART. III. The most excellent lords the plenipotentiaries promise and take upon themselves, that their above named masters shall ratify this treaty; and within the space of two months the ratification shall be exchanged.
p5.zh: ART. (英语). 三. 方案 最杰出的全权代表们许诺并承担自己的责任,他们上面提到的主人们应批准这项条约;在两个月之内,应交换批准文书。

p6.original: By this treaty, the crown of Portugal becomes bound to admit the English woollens upon the same footing as before the prohibition; that is, not to raise the duties which had been paid before that time. But it does not become bound to admit them upon any better terms than those of any other nation, of France or Holland, for example. The crown of Great Britain, on the contrary, becomes bound to admit the wines of Portugal, upon paying only two-thirds of the duty which is paid for those of France, the wines most likely to come into competition with them. So far this treaty, therefore, is evidently advantageous to Portugal, and disadvantageous to Great Britain.
p6.zh: 根据这项条约,葡萄牙王室有义务接受英国羊毛兰,其地位与禁令之前相同;也就是说,不得提高当时已经支付的义务。 但是,它没有义务以比任何其他国家,例如法国或荷兰更好的条件接纳他们。 相反,大不列颠王冠在只支付法国王冠所付义务的三分之二后,就有义务接受葡萄牙的葡萄酒,而法国王冠最有可能与之竞争。 因此,到目前为止,这项条约显然对葡萄牙有利,对大不列颠不利。

p7.original: It has been celebrated, however, as a masterpiece of the commercial policy of England. Portugal receives annually from the Brazils a greater quantity of gold than can be employed in its domestic commerce, whether in the shape of coin or of plate. The surplus is too valuable to be allowed to lie idle and locked up in coffers; and as it can find no advantageous market at home, it must, notwithstanding; any prohibition, be sent abroad, and exchanged for something for which there is a more advantageous market at home. A large share of it comes annually to England, in return either for English goods, or for those of other European nations that receive their returns through England. Mr Barretti was informed, that the weekly packet-boat from Lisbon brings, one week with another, more than £50,000 in gold to England. The sum had probably been exaggerated. It would amount to more than £2,600,000 a year, which is more than the Brazils are supposed to afford.
p7.zh: 然而,它作为英国商业政策的杰作而被庆祝. 葡萄牙每年从巴西获得的黄金数量比在国内商业中可以使用的多,无论是硬币还是板块。盈余太宝贵,不能让闲置和锁在国库里;由于不能在国内找到有利市场,尽管有任何禁令,必须将其送到国外,并交换一些在国内有更有利市场的东西。 其中很大一部分每年来英国,要么是换取英国货物,要么是那些通过英国获得回报的其他欧洲国家的货物. 巴雷蒂先生被告知,每周从里斯本送来的包船 一周后,会给英国带来超过5万英镑的黄金。这笔数额可能被夸大了。 每年将超过2,600,000英镑,这比巴西人应该承担的要多。

p8.original: Our merchants were, some years ago, out of humour with the crown of Portugal. Some privileges which had been granted them, not by treaty, but by the free grace of that crown, at the solicitation, indeed, it is probable, and in return for much greater favours, defence and protection from the crown of Great Britain, had been either infringed or revoked. The people, therefore, usually most interested in celebrating the Portugal trade, were then rather disposed to represent it as less advantageous than it had commonly been imagined. The far greater part, almost the whole, they pretended, of this annual importation of gold, was not on account of Great Britain, but of other European nations; the fruits and wines of Portugal annually imported into Great Britain nearly compensating the value of the British goods sent thither.
p8.zh: 我们的商人,几年前, 与葡萄牙的王冠, 不合幽默。 有些特权不是通过条约,而是通过该王室的自由恩惠给予的,在索取时,的确有可能,作为回报,大不列颠王室的保护和防卫要么遭到侵犯,要么被取消。 因此,人们通常对庆祝葡萄牙贸易最感兴趣,但后来却倾向于将葡萄牙视为比人们通常想象的更不利的贸易。 他们假装,每年进口黄金的绝大部分,几乎全部并非是大不列颠,而是其他欧洲国家;葡萄牙每年进口到大不列颠的水果和葡萄酒几乎补偿了英国寄来的黄金的价值。

p9.original: Let us suppose, however, that the whole was on account of Great Britain, and that it amounted to a still greater sum than Mr Barretti seems to imagine; this trade would not, upon that account, be more advantageous than any other, in which, for the same value sent out, we received an equal value of consumable goods in return.
p9.zh: 然而,让我们假设,整个交易都是因为大不列颠造成的,而且其数额仍然比巴雷蒂先生所想象的要大;这种交易不会比任何其他交易更有利,因为出于同样的价值,我们得到了同样价值的消费品作为回报。

p10.original: It is but a very small part of this importation which, it can be supposed, is employed as an annual addition, either to the plate or to the coin of the kingdom. The rest must all be sent abroad, and exchanged for consumable goods of some kind or other. But if those consumable goods were purchased directly with the produce of English industry, it would be more for the advantage of England, than first to purchase with that produce the gold of Portugal, and afterwards to purchase with that gold those consumable goods. A direct foreign trade of consumption is always more advantageous than a round-about one; and to bring the same value of foreign goods to the home market requires a much smaller capital in the one way than in the ether. If a smaller share of its industry, therefore, had been employed in producing goods fit for the Portugal market, and a greater in producing those lit for the other markets, where those consumable goods for which there is a demand in Great Britain are to be had, it would have been more for the advantage of England. To procure both the gold which it wants for its own use, and the consumable goods, would, in this way, employ a much smaller capital than at present. There would be a spare capital, therefore, to be employed for other purposes, in exciting an additional quantity of industry, and in raising a greater annual produce.
p10.zh: 这仅仅是这种进口品的一小部分,可以假定,它被作为年度添加,无论是在板块上还是在王国的硬币上。其余的必须全部送到国外,并交换某种或其他消耗性货物。 但是,如果这些消耗性商品是直接与英国工业的产品一起购买的,则更有利于英国,而不是首先与葡萄牙黄金生产者一起购买,然后与黄金一起购买这些消耗性商品。直接的对外消费贸易总是比环绕消费贸易更有利;要使外国商品的价值与国内市场持平,需要比乙醚的资本要小得多。 因此,如果在生产适合葡萄牙市场的货物时,其工业的份额较小,而生产其他市场所需的产品的比例更大,而那些大不列颠有需求可消费的货物则更有利于英格兰。以这种方式采购自己想要的黄金和消耗品将比目前少得多的资本。 因此,为了其他目的、为了刺激更多的工业以及为了提高年产量,将有一个多余的资本。

p11.original: Though Britain were entirely excluded from the Portugal trade, it could find very little difficulty in procuring all the annual supplies of gold which it wants, either for the purposes of plate, or of coin, or of foreign trade. Gold, like every other commodity, is always somewhere or another to be got for its value by those who have that value to give for it. The annual surplus of gold in Portugal, besides, would still be sent abroad, and though not carried away by Great Britain, would be carried away by some other nation, which would be glad to sell it again for its price, in the same manner as Great Britain does at present. In buying gold of Portugal, indeed, we buy it at the first hand; whereas, in buying it of any other nation, except Spain, we should buy it at the second, and might pay somewhat dearer. This difference, however, would surely be too insignificant to deserve the public attention.
p11.zh: 虽然英国完全被排除在葡萄牙贸易之外,但它在采购其每年想要的所有黄金供应方面,无论是为盘子、硬币或外贸目的,都没有什么困难。黄金与其他商品一样,总是被那些有这种价值的人从某个地方或另一个地方得到。 此外,葡萄牙每年的黄金盈余仍将寄往国外,虽然不是被大不列颠带走,而是被一些其他国家带走,它们愿意以英国目前同样的方式再次出售黄金,以换取其价格。 事实上,在购买葡萄牙的黄金时,我们一手购买;而在购买除西班牙以外的任何其他国家黄金时,我们应该在第二手购买黄金,并可能支付一些更多的费用。 然而,这种差别肯定太小,不值得公众注意。

p12.original: Almost all our gold, it is said, comes from Portugal. With other nations, the balance of trade is either against as, or not much in our favour. But we should remember, that the more gold we import from one country, the less we must necessarily import from all others. The effectual demand for gold, like that for every other commodity, is in every country limited to a certain quantity. If nine-tenths of this quantity are imported from one country, there remains a tenth only to be imported from all others. The more gold, besides, that is annually imported from some particular countries, over and above what is requisite for plate and for coin, the more must necessarily be exported to some others: and the more that most insignificant object of modern policy, the balance of trade, appears to be in our favour with some particular countries, the more it must necessarily appear to be against us with many others.
p12.zh: 据说,我们几乎所有的黄金都来自葡萄牙。与其他国家相比,贸易平衡要么是相反的,要么不是对我们有利。 但我们应该记住,我们从一个国家进口的黄金越多,我们就越不必从所有其他国家进口黄金。 对黄金的实际需求,如同对所有其他商品的需求一样,在每个国家仅限于一定数量。 如果这批货物中有九十分之一是从一个国家进口的,则只有十分之一只能从所有其他国家进口。 此外,每年从某些特定国家进口的黄金越多,除了对硬币和硬币的需求之外,也必须向另一些国家出口的黄金就越多:现代政策中最微不足道的目标,贸易平衡,似乎对一些特定国家有利,而与许多其他国家相比,它也必然对我们不利。

p13.original: It was upon this silly notion, however, that England could not subsist without the Portugal trade, that, towards the end of the late war, France and Spain, without pretending either offence or provocation, required the king of Portugal to exclude all British ships from his ports, and, for the security of this exclusion, to receive into them French or Spanish garrisons. Had the king of Portugal submitted to those ignominious terms which his brother-in-law the king of Spain proposed to him, Britain would have been freed from a much greater inconveniency than the loss of the Portugal trade, the burden of supporting a very weak ally, so unprovided of every thing for his own defence, that the whole power of England, had it been directed to that single purpose, could scarce, perhaps, have defended him for another campaign. The loss of the Portugal trade would, no doubt, have occasioned a considerable embarrassment to the merchants at that time engaged in it, who might not, perhaps, have found out, for a year or two, any other equally advantageous method of employing their capitals; and in this would probably have consisted all the inconveniency which England could have suffered from this notable piece of commercial policy.
p13.zh: 然而,正是基于这一愚蠢的概念,没有葡萄牙的贸易,英格兰是无法生存的,在战争末期,法国和西班牙在不假装犯罪或挑衅的情况下,要求葡萄牙国王将所有英国船只排除在其港口之外,为了这一排除的安全起见,接受法国或西班牙驻军。 如果葡萄牙国王服从西班牙国王的姐夫向他提出的这些可耻条件,那么,英国本来会摆脱比葡萄牙贸易的损失更大的不便,因为葡萄牙贸易的损失是支持一个非常弱小的盟友的负担,如此不为他自己的防卫而提供一切,以致整个英格兰的势力,如果被指向这个单一的目的,可能就少之又少了,也许,为他的另一战役辩护了. 毫无疑问,葡萄牙贸易的丧失会给当时从事贸易的商人带来相当的尴尬,他们也许在一两年的时间里没有发现使用首都的任何其他同样有利的方法;在这点上,很可能包括英格兰可能因这一引人注目的商业政策而遭受的所有不便。

p14.original: The great annual importation of gold and silver is neither for the purpose of plate nor of coin, but of foreign trade. A round-about foreign trade of consumption can be carried on more advantageously by means of these metals than of almost any other goods. As they are the universal instruments of commerce, they are more readily received in return for all commodities than any other goods; and, on account of their small bulk and great value, it costs less to transport them backward and forward from one place to another than almost any other sort of merchandize, and they lose less of their value by being so transported. Of all the commodities, therefore, which are bought in one foreign country, for no other purpose but to be sold or exchanged again for some other goods in another, there are none so convenient as gold and silver. In facilitating all the different round-about foreign trades of consumption which are carried on in Great Britain, consists the principal advantage of the Portugal trade; and though it is not a capital advantage, it is, no doubt, a considerable one.
p14.zh: 每年大量进口金银既非板块目的,也非硬币目的,而是外贸目的.与几乎所有其他商品相比,通过这些金属进行的环形对外消费贸易更有利。 由于它们是世界商业工具,它们比其他任何商品更容易得到所有商品的回报;由于它们的批量小,价值巨大,将它们从一个地方往后运送和从另一个地方往前转运的成本比其他任何种类的商品要低,它们由于被这样运输而损失的价值也更少。 因此,在一个外国购买的所有商品中,除了在另一外国出售或交换其他一些商品之外,没有其他商品比黄金和白银更方便。 在便利大不列颠进行的所有不同的环绕路线的对外消费贸易方面,葡萄牙贸易的主要优势;尽管这不是资本优势,但无疑是相当大的优势。

p15.original: That any annual addition which, it can reasonably be supposed, is made either to the plate or to the coin of the kingdom, could require but a very small annual importation of gold and silver, seems evident enough; and though we had no direct trade with Portugal, this small quantity could always, somewhere or another, be very easily got.
p15.zh: 任何可以合理假定的年增量,无论是在纸牌上还是在王国的硬币上,只要每年进口很少的金银,似乎都足够明显;尽管我们与葡萄牙没有直接贸易,但这种少量数量总是很容易得到的。

p16.original: Though the goldsmiths trade be very considerable in Great Britain, the far greater part of the new plate which they annually sell, is made from other old plate melted down; so that the addition annually made to the whole plate of the kingdom cannot be very great, and could require but a very small annual importation.
p16.zh: 虽然金匠贸易在大不列颠相当可观,但他们每年销售的新板块中,很大一部分是用其他旧板块熔化而成的;因此每年对王国整个板块的添加量不可能很大,可能只需要非常小的年进口量.

p17.original: It is the same case with the coin. Nobody imagines, I believe, that even the greater part of the annual coinage, amounting, for ten years together, before the late reformation of the gold coin, to upwards of £800,000 a-year in gold, was an annual addition to the money before current in the kingdom. In a country where the expense of the coinage is defrayed by the government, the value of the coin, even when it contains its full standard weight of gold and silver, can never be much greater than that of an equal quantity of those metals uncoined, because it requires only the trouble of going to the mint, and the delay, perhaps, of a few weeks, to procure for any quantity of uncoined gold and silver an equal quantity of those metals in coin; but in every country the greater part of the current coin is almost always more or less worn, or otherwise degenerated from its standard. In Great Britain it was, before the late reformation, a good deal so, the gold being more than two per cent., and the silver more than eight per cent. below its standard weight. But if forty-four guineas and a-half, containing their full standard weight, a pound weight of gold, could purchase very little more than a pound weight of uncoined gold; forty-four guineas and a-half, wanting a part of their weight, could not purchase a pound weight, and something was to be added, in order to make up the deficiency. The current price of gold bullion at market, therefore, instead of being the same with the mint price, or £46:14:6, was then about £47:14s., and sometimes about £48. When the greater part of the coin, however, was in this degenerate condition, forty four guineas and a-half, fresh from the mint, would purchase no more goods in the market than any other ordinary guineas; because, when they came into the coffers of the merchant, being confounded with other money, they could not afterwards be distinguished without more trouble than the difference was worth. Like other guineas, they were worth no more than £46:14:6. If thrown into the melting pot, however, they produced, without any sensible loss, a pound weight of standard gold, which could be sold at any time for between £47:14s. and £48, either in gold or silver, as fit for all the purposes of coin as that which had been melted down. There was an evident profit, therefore, in melting down new-coined money; and it was done so instantaneously, that no precaution of government could prevent it. The operations of the mint were, upon this account, somewhat like the web of Penelope; the work that was done in the day was undone in the night. The mint was employed, not so much in making daily additions to the coin, as in replacing the very best part of it, which was daily melted down.
p17.zh: 硬币也是这样 我认为,没有人会想到,即使年度硬币的大部分, 在金币晚期改革之前的十年里, 每年都会增加80万英镑的金币, 也就是在王国现钞之前的一年。在一个硬币费用由政府支付的国家里,硬币的价值,即使包含金银的全部标准重量,也永远不能比那些没有硬币的金属数量相等的多,因为它只需要去薄荷的麻烦,以及拖延,也许几周的时间来采购任何数量的未硬币中的金银,这些金属的数量相等;但是在每个国家,现在的硬币的大部分几乎总是或多或少地磨损,或者从标准上堕落. 在大不列颠,在改革后期之前,这是一笔不错的生意,黄金占2%以上,银占8%以上,低于标准重量。 但是如果四十四个豚鼠和半兽鼠, 包含它们的全部标准重量,一磅的黄金重量, 能够买到很少的超过一磅的无铜黄金重量; 四十四个豚鼠和半兽鼠, 想要一部分的重量, 无法买到一磅的重量, 并且应该加上一些东西, 来弥补不足。 因此,现时市场上的金牛顿价格与薄荷价格不同,即46:14:6英镑,当时大约是47:14英镑,有时大约是48英镑. 然而,当硬币的较大部分处于这种衰落状态时,从薄荷中新鲜出来的四十四个豚鼠和半个豚鼠在市场上购买的商品不会比其他普通豚鼠多;因为当它们进入商家的国库时,由于与其他钱搞混,在之后没有比差价更多的麻烦,它们无法区分.和其他豚鼠一样,它们的价值不超过46:14:6. 但是,如果扔进熔炉,它们会生产出一磅标准金,没有任何合理的损失,在47:14至48英镑的时间内,可以随时以金或银两种形式出售,这与已经熔化的硬币一样适合所有硬币用途. 因此,在融化新货币方面,显然有益处;而且,这是瞬间发生的,政府没有任何预防措施可以阻止这种情况。薄荷的操作,就这个说法而言,有点像Penelope的网络;白天完成的工作在夜间被取消。薄荷币被使用,在每天制造硬币添加量方面,没有太多,比如用来取代其最精美的部分,而该部分每天都被熔化.

p18.original: Were the private people who carry their gold and silver to the mint to pay themselves for the coinage, it would add to the value of those metals, in the same manner as the fashion does to that of plate. Coined gold and silver would be more valuable than uncoined. The seignorage, if it was not exorbitant, would add to the bullion the whole value of the duty; because, the government having everywhere the exclusive privilege of coining, no coin can come to market cheaper than they think proper to afford it. If the duty was exorbitant, indeed, that is, if it was very much above the real value of the labour and expense requisite for coinage, false coiners, both at home and abroad, might be encouraged, by the great difference between the value of bullion and that of coin, to pour in so great a quantity of counterfeit money as might reduce the value of the government money. In France, however, though the seignorage is eight per cent., no sensible inconveniency of this kind is found to arise from it. The dangers to which a false coiner is everywhere exposed, if he lives in the country of which he counterfeits the coin, and to which his agents or correspondents are exposed, if he lives in a foreign country, are by far too great to be incurred for the sake of a profit of six or seven per cent.
p18.zh: 如果那些把金银带到薄荷上 以支付硬币的私人 将会增加这些金属的价值 与时尚一样铜制的金银比没有铜制的更值钱.铸币局如果不是过高的话,会增加这项义务的全部价值;因为,政府无论在任何地方都有硬币的专属特权,任何硬币都不可能比他们认为合适的价格便宜。 如果这项义务过高,也就是说,如果它大大高于硬币所需的劳动力和费用的实际价值,那么,无论在国内外,由于金块价值与硬币价值之间的巨大差异,可能会鼓励假币公司投入大量假币,从而可能降低政府货币的价值。 然而,在法国,尽管铸造率为8%,但没有发现这种不方便的情况。假币师在任何地方都暴露出的危险,如果他住在他伪造硬币的国家,而他的代理人或通讯员在外国也暴露出的危险,为了六或7%的利润,已经太过严重了.

p19.original: The seignorage in France raises the value of the coin higher than in proportion to the quantity of pure gold which it contains. Thus, by the edict of January 1726, the mint price of fine gold of twenty-four carats was fixed at seven hundred and forty livres nine sous and one denier one-eleventh the mark of eight Paris ounces. {See Dictionnaire des Monnoies, tom. ii. article Seigneurage, p. 439, par 81. Abbot de Bazinghen, Conseiller-Commissaire en la Cour des Monnoies à Paris.} The gold coin of France, making an allowance for the remedy of the mint, contains twenty-one carats and three-fourths of fine gold, and two carats one-fourth of alloy. The mark of standard gold, therefore, is worth no more than about six hundred and seventy-one livres ten deniers. But in France this mark of standard gold is coined into thirty louis d'ors of twenty-four livres each, or into seven hundred and twenty livres. The coinage, therefore, increases the value of a mark of standard gold bullion, by the difference between six hundred and seventy-one livres ten deniers and seven hundred and twenty livres, or by forty-eight livres nineteen sous and two deniers.
p19.zh: 法国的铸币使硬币价值高于其包含的纯金数量的比例. 因此,根据1726年1月的法令,24克拉精美金币的薄荷价格被定为740里弗尔9索乌斯,巴黎8盎司的标记为1分之11。439,第81段。 法国的金币,为薄荷的补救提供了补贴,包含21克拉和四分之三的精制金币,以及两克拉的四分之一合金。 因此,标准金的印记价值不超过六百七十一里弗斯十名否认者. 但是在法国,这个标准金的标记被铸成每枚24里弗尔的30 louis d'ors,或者铸成720里弗尔. 因此,硬币增加了标准金金币的印记价值,差值为六百七十一里弗斯十德尼和七百二十里弗斯,或四十八利弗斯十九德索斯和二德尼.

p20.original: A seignorage will, in many cases, take away altogether, and will in all cases diminish, the profit of melting down the new coin. This profit always arises from the difference between the quantity of bullion which the common currency ought to contain and that which it actually does contain. If this difference is less than the seignorage, there will be loss instead of profit. If it is equal to the seignorage, there will be neither profit nor loss. If it is greater than the seignorage, there will, indeed, be some profit, but less than if there was no seignorage. If, before the late reformation of the gold coin, for example, there had been a seignorage of five per cent. upon the coinage, there would have been a loss of three per cent. upon the melting down of the gold coin. If the seignorage had been two per cent., there would have been neither profit nor loss. If the seignorage had been one per cent., there would have been a profit but of one per cent. only, instead of two per cent. Wherever money is received by tale, therefore, and not by weight, a seignorage is the most effectual preventive of the melting down of the coin, and, for the same reason, of its exportation. It is the best and heaviest pieces that are commonly either melted down or exported, because it is upon such that the largest profits are made.
p20.zh: 在许多情况下,一个铸币局会完全夺走,而且无论如何都会减少熔化新硬币的利润。 这种利润总是来自共同货币应包含的金块数量与它实际包含的金块数量之间的差额。 如果这种差别小于铸币局,就会有亏损而不是利润. 若与铸物相等,则既无损益. 若其大于铸造,则确实有一定利润,但比无铸造者少. 例如,如果在金币改革晚期之前,铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸局铸局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸局铸局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局铸币局的铸币局 如果铸造为2%,就不会有利润或损失。 如果铸造率为1%,本来只有1%的利润,而不是2%。 因此,无论从故事中而不是从重量中收到钱财,铸币是硬币熔化的最有效预防手段,也是出于同样的原因出口硬币。 这是通常融化或出口的最优和最重的棋子,因为最大的利润是在这种棋子上。

p21.original: The law for the encouragement of the coinage, by rendering it duty-free, was first enacted during the reign of Charles II. for a limited time, and afterwards continued, by different prolongations, till 1769, when it was rendered perpetual. The bank of England, in order to replenish their coffers with money, are frequently obliged to carry bullion to the mint; and it was more for their interest, they probably imagined, that the coinage should be at the expense of the government than at their own. It was probably out of complaisance to this great company, that the government agreed to render this law perpetual. Should the custom of weighing gold, however, come to be disused, as it is very likely to be on account of its inconveniency; should the gold coin of England come to be received by tale, as it was before the late recoinage this great company may, perhaps, find that they have, upon this, as upon some other occasions, mistaken their own interest not a little.
p21.zh: 通过使硬币免税来鼓励铸币的法律,最初是在查理二世统治期间颁布的,时间有限,之后又通过不同的延长延续,直到1769年它被永久化.英格兰银行为了用钱来补充国库,经常不得不将金块带到薄荷上;他们可能想象,这更是为了他们的利益,即硬币应该牺牲政府而不是他们自己的利益. 政府同意将这部法律永久化 很可能是出于对这个伟大公司的顺从 但是,如果衡金的习惯不再使用,因为它非常可能不方便;如果英格兰的金币是按故事来接收的,就像晚期重新铸币之前那样,这个伟大的公司也许会发现,他们在这一点上,正如在其他场合一样,没有多少地误解了他们自己的利益。

p22.original: Before the late recoinage, when the gold currency of England was two per cent. below its standard weight, as there was no seignorage, it was two per cent. below the value of that quantity of standard gold bullion which it ought to have contained. When this great company, therefore, bought gold bullion in order to have it coined, they were obliged to pay for it two per cent. more than it was worth after the coinage. But if there had been a seignorage of two per cent. upon the coinage, the common gold currency, though two per cent. below its standard weight, would, notwithstanding, have been equal in value to the quantity of standard gold which it ought to have contained; the value of the fashion compensating in this case the diminution of the weight. They would, indeed, have had the seignorage to pay, which being two per cent., their loss upon the whole transaction would have been two per cent., exactly the same, but no greater than it actually was.
p22.zh: 在晚期重新铸币之前,英格兰的黄金货币为2%,低于其标准重量,因为没有铸币,低于2%,低于其本应包含的标准金金币的数量。 因此,当这个伟大的公司为了铸造金块而购买金块时,他们不得不支付2%的金块,比硬币铸造后的价值还要高。 但是,如果硬币上有2%的铸币,那么,低于标准重量的普通金币,尽管只有2%,但价值与它本应包含的标准金币数量相等;在这种情况下,补偿重量缩减的时尚价值。 他们确实会得到2%的代号,他们对整个交易的损失是2%,完全相同,但并不比实际损失大。

p23.original: If the seignorage had been five per cent. and the gold currency only two per cent. below its standard weight, the bank would, in this case, have gained three per cent. upon the price of the bullion; but as they would have had a seignorage of five per cent. to pay upon the coinage, their loss upon the whole transaction would, in the same manner, have been exactly two per cent.
p23.zh: 如果铸币局的铸币为5%.,而金币仅低于其标准重量的2%.,在这种情况下,银行根据金币的价格将获得3%.,但是,由于它们本来会有5%的铸币局来支付硬币,它们对整个交易的损失同样是2%.

p24.original: If the seignorage had been only one per cent., and the gold currency two per cent. below its standard weight, the bank would, in this case, have lost only one per cent. upon the price of the bullion; but as they would likewise have had a seignorage of one per cent. to pay, their loss upon the whole transaction would have been exactly two per cent., in the same manner as in all other cases.
p24.zh: 如果铸币局只支付1%.,而金币低于标准重量2%.,在这种情况下,银行只支付1%.;但同样,银行也要支付1%.的铸币局,则整个交易的损失为2%.,与所有其他情况相同。

p25.original: If there was a reasonable seignorage, while at the same time the coin contained its full standard weight, as it has done very nearly since the late recoinage, whatever the bank might lose by the seignorage, they would gain upon the price of the bullion; and whatever they might gain upon the price of the bullion, they would lose by the seignorage. They would neither lose nor gain, therefore, upon the whole transaction, and they would in this, as in all the foregoing cases, be exactly in the same situation as if there was no seignorage.
p25.zh: 如果有一个合理的铸币局,同时硬币中包含其全部标准重量,就像它从晚期铸币局开始就已经做的一样,无论银行因铸币局可能损失什么,它们都会从金刚币的价格中获利;无论它们从金刚币的价格中获利什么,它们都会因为铸币局的损失而损失. 因此,他们不会在整笔交易上失去或获利,他们将象上述所有情况一样,处于与没有抵押品的情况完全相同的境地。

p26.original: When the tax upon a commodity is so moderate as not to encourage smuggling, the merchant who deals in it, though he advances, does not properly pay the tax, as he gets it back in the price of the commodity. The tax is finally paid by the last purchaser or consumer. But money is a commodity, with regard to which every man is a merchant. Nobody buys it but in order to sell it again; and with regard to it there is, in ordinary cases, no last purchaser or consumer. When the tax upon coinage, therefore, is so moderate as not to encourage false coining, though every body advances the tax, nobody finally pays it; because every body gets it back in the advanced value of the coin.
p26.zh: 当对商品的征税如此温和,以至于不鼓励走私时,交易商虽然提速,但并没有适当缴纳税款,因为他在商品价格中得到了回扣.最终由最后的购买者或消费者缴纳税款. 但是金钱是一种商品,在这个商品上,每个人都是商人. 没有人买它,但是为了再次出售它;在一般情况下,没有最后的购买者或消费者。 因此,当硬币的税收如此温和,以至于不鼓励假币,虽然每个机构都会推进税收,但最终没有人支付;因为每个机构都以硬币的高级价值获得.

p27.original: A moderate seignorage, therefore, would not, in any case, augment the expense of the bank, or of any other private persons who carry their bullion to the mint in order to be coined; and the want of a moderate seignorage does not in any case diminish it. Whether there is or is not a seignorage, if the currency contains its full standard weight, the coinage costs nothing to anybody; and if it is short of that weight, the coinage must always cost the difference between the quantity of bullion which ought to be contained in it, and that which actually is contained in it.
p27.zh: 因此,温和的铸币无论如何不会增加银行或任何其他私人的费用,他们为了铸造硬币而将金块运到薄荷;温和的铸币的匮乏在任何情况下都不会减少。 无论是否存在铸币局,如果货币包含其全部标准重量,硬币对任何人都不产生任何代价;如果硬币低于该重量,硬币必须总是花费其中应该包含的金块数量与实际包含在其中的金块数量之间的差额。

p28.original: The government, therefore, when it defrays the expense of coinage, not only incurs some small expense, but loses some small revenue which it might get by a proper duty; and neither the bank, nor any other private persons, are in the smallest degree benefited by this useless piece of public generosity.
p28.zh: 因此,当政府支付硬币费用时,不仅产生一些小费用,而且损失一些小收入,而政府可能通过适当的职责获得这些收入;银行或任何其他私人,在最小的程度上都没有从这种无用的公众慷慨中获得好处。

p29.original: The directors of the bank, however, would probably be unwilling to agree to the imposition of a seignorage upon the authority of a speculation which promises them no gain, but only pretends to insure them from any loss. In the present state of the gold coin, and as long as it continues to be received by weight, they certainly would gain nothing by such a change. But if the custom of weighing the gold coin should ever go into disuse, as it is very likely to do, and if the gold coin should ever fall into the same state of degradation in which it was before the late recoinage, the gain, or more properly the savings, of the bank, inconsequence of the imposition of a seignorage, would probably be very considerable. The bank of England is the only company which sends any considerable quantity of bullion to the mint, and the burden of the annual coinage falls entirely, or almost entirely, upon it. If this annual coinage had nothing to do but to repair the unavoidable losses and necessary wear and tear of the coin, it could seldom exceed fifty thousand, or at most a hundred thousand pounds. But when the coin is degraded below its standard weight, the annual coinage must, besides this, fill up the large vacuities which exportation and the melting pot are continually making in the current coin. It was upon this account, that during the ten or twelve years immediately preceding the late reformation of the gold coin, the annual coinage amounted, at an average, to more than £850,000. But if there had been a seignorage of four or five per cent. upon the gold coin, it would probably, even in the state in which things then were, have put an effectual stop to the business both of exportation and of the melting pot. The bank, instead of losing every year about two and a half per cent. upon the bullion which was to be coined into more than eight hundred and fifty thousand pounds, or incurring an annual loss of more than £21,250 pounds, would not probably have incurred the tenth part of that loss.
p29.zh: 然而,银行董事们可能不愿意同意将一种投机行为强加于他们,而这种投机行为保证他们不会获利,而只是假装保证他们不会遭受任何损失。 在金币的目前状态下,只要金币继续按重量得到,它们肯定不会因为这样的改变而得到任何好处. 但是,如果金币的权重习惯像它极有可能那样永远不再使用,如果金币会像晚期重新铸币之前一样堕落,那么银行的收益,或更适当的储蓄,强制铸币的不规则后果,很可能是非常可观的.英国银行是唯一一家向薄荷薄荷公司送出任何相当数量的金块的公司,每年的硬币负担完全或几乎全部落在它身上. 如果这个年度硬币除了修复硬币不可避免的损失和必要的磨损之外,没有其他事可做,那么它很少能超过5万,或者最多可以超过10万磅. 但当硬币退化到低于标准重量时,除此以外,年硬币必须充斥出口和熔炉在现今硬币中不断制造的大挥发量. 正是在这一说法下,在金币晚期改制前的10年或12年里,年币平均超过85万英镑. 但是,如果金币上有4%或5%的铸币,那么,即使在当时的状况下,它也有可能使出口和熔炉的业务都停止。银行没有每年损失约2.5万英镑,而是在准备铸成85万多英镑或每年损失超过21 250英镑的金块上,很可能不会造成损失的第十部分。

p30.original: The revenue allotted by parliament for defraying the expense of the coinage is but fourteen thousand pounds a-year; and the real expense which it costs the government, or the fees of the officers of the mint, do not, upon ordinary occasions, I am assured, exceed the half of that sum. The saving of so very small a sum, or even the gaining of another, which could not well be much larger, are objects too inconsiderable, it may be thought, to deserve the serious attention of government. But the saving of eighteen or twenty thousand pounds a-year, in case of an event which is not improbable, which has frequently happened before, and which is very likely to happen again, is surely an object which well deserves the serious attention, even of so great a company as the bank of England.
p30.zh: 议会每年用于支付硬币费用的收入只有14,000英镑;而且,它给政府造成的实际费用,或薄荷币官员的费用,在通常情况下,我确信不会超过这一数额的一半。节省如此小的一笔钱,甚至获得另一笔钱,可能不会大得多,这些物品太少,也许可以认为,值得政府认真注意。 但是,每年节省一万八千或二万英镑,以防发生以前经常发生的,而且很可能再次发生的事件,肯定是一个值得认真注意的对象,即使是像英国银行这样伟大的公司也值得认真注意。

p31.original: Some of the foregoing reasonings and observations might, perhaps, have been more properly placed in those chapters of the first book which treat of the origin and use of money, and of the difference between the real and the nominal price of commodities. But as the law for the encouragement of coinage derives its origin from those vulgar prejudices which have been introduced by the mercantile system, I judged it more proper to reserve them for this chapter. Nothing could be more agreeable to the spirit of that system than a sort of bounty upon the production of money, the very thing which, it supposes, constitutes the wealth of every nation. It is one of its many admirable expedients for enriching the country.
p31.zh: 上文的一些推理和意见也许更适合放在第一本关于货币的来源和使用以及商品的实际价格和名义价格之间的差别的章节中。 但是,由于鼓励硬币的法律来源于商贸制度所引入的粗俗偏见,我判断将它们保留在本章更为恰当。没有什么比这种制度的精神更能接受的了,那就是对生产金钱的某种奖励,它认为,这种报酬是每个国家的财富。 这是它丰富国家的许多令人钦佩的捷径之一。
